- Switched to pure-Go SQLite driver, CGO is no longer required to compile Gogs. [#7882](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/7882)
- Support using TLS for Redis session provider using `[session] PROVIDER_CONFIG = ...,tls=true`. [#7860](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/7860)
- Support expanading values in `app.ini` from environment variables, e.g. `[database] PASSWORD = ${DATABASE_PASSWORD}`. [#8057](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8057)
- 500 error on repository watchers and stargazers pages when using MS

gh-ost v1.1.11 includes MariaDB support, StatsD metrics, improved binlog processing, and several reliability and release/build improvements.
- **MariaDB and MariaDB GTID support** ([#1724](https://github.com/github/gh-ost/pull/1724), [#1731](https://github.com/github/gh-ost/pull/1731)) by @conf: Adds automatic server-flavor detection, MariaDB-specific replication behavior and privileges, and MariaDB GTID migrations. CI covers MariaDB 10.5, 10.6, 10.11, 11.4, and 11.8.
- **Multi-flavor replica-test harness**

## 📝 What's Changed

**Added option to skip Pongo migration hash check.** This could cause some friction if someone (like me) accidentally changed whitespace in a migration script. Now you can pass `{ ignoreMigrationHashMismatch: true }` through migrate options, and the migration hash check will be disabled. What's more, it'll override the migration hash (if it existed).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/event-driven-io/Pongo/compare/0.16.4...0.16.5
- On PostgreSQL, produces to different partitions run concurrently, and the new `pool_max_size` storage URL option sets the connection pool size.

- On PostgreSQL, SQLite and Turso, a consumer no longer stalls on a record larger than its fetch limit.
- Topics set to `message.timestamp.type=LogAppendTime` get the broker's timestamps, in records, Produce responses, timestamp lookups (except on SlateDB) and lake tables.
- Rollback: don't roll back a PostgreSQL, SQLite or Turso broker with `LogAppendTime` topics, and restart producers that bumped their epoch after rolling back.

Nisshi 0.8.0 brings retention, message-size, ListOffsets and consumer-group behaviour closer to Apache Kafka, and deprecates the SlateDB engine. It has upgrade notes that need action before you upgrade, especially for retention on PostgreSQL and SQLite.
- PostgreSQL Fetch and the retention and compaction sweeps no longer scan the whole `record` table, so a fetch's cost no longer grows with the backlog.
- The `slatedb://` engine is deprecated; it accepts only security fixes and may be removed in a future rel

Pre-release of 0.8.0, for trying changes before it ships: behaviour and storage formats can still change, so use the [latest release](https://github.com/nisshi-io/nisshi/releases/latest) for anything you keep. See [Which release to use](https://github.com/nisshi-io/nisshi#which-release-to-use).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/nisshi-io/nisshi/compare/v0.7.0...v0.8.0-pre.1

- PostgreSQL aborts timed-out transactions, so an abandoned transaction no longer stalls `read_committed` consumers.
- The broker creates the PostgreSQL and SQLite schema at startup and records its version, so a new deployment needs no setup step.
Nisshi 0.7.0 is the first stable release since the project was renamed from Tansu. Nisshi is a stateless, Apache Kafka-compatible broker with PostgreSQL, SQLite, S3, Google Cloud Storage, SlateDB and in-memory storage.
